headline: SCOPE reports joint capability and safety post-training for computer-use agents
summary: An arXiv preprint presents SCOPE, a post-training recipe for computer-use agents that combines capability demonstrations, safe continuations around environmental hazards, explicit refusals and subsequent capability RL. On Qwen3.5-9B, the authors report 54.17% OSWorld task success and 64.30% OS-BLIND attack avoidance after RL, with a 58.80% harmonic mean in their benchmark setting. Matched-step ablations suggest refusal trajectories contribute most of the measured attack-avoidance gain, while safe-continuation trajectories better preserve task utility. These are author-reported results on one model and benchmark suite; OS-BLIND does not distinguish safe continuation from refusal or incidental task failure, and the aggregate is not a deployment safety guarantee.
